question: What three types of signs are required at an interchange exit-ramp terminal where wrong-way entry could inadvertently occur?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Based on the visual evidence, the three types of regulatory signs used at an exit-ramp termination to deter wrong-way entry are DO NOT ENTER (R5-1), WRONG WAY (R5-1a), and ONE WAY (R6-1/R6-2) signs. The DO NOT ENTER sign is expressly mandated at the intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad, and Figure 2B-15 illustrates the coordinated placement of all three sign types (along with STOP or YIELD control at the ramp terminal). Note that the text evidence supplied does not include the Section 2B.48 Standard itself, so the full mandatory wording for the WRONG WAY and ONE WAY signs at this location cannot be quoted from the provided text excerpts. Standards (mandatory): - As shown in the page image containing Section 2B.46: "The DO NOT ENTER (R5-1) sign (see Figure 2B-13) shall be used at the following locations: … B. The intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad as specified in Section 2B.48 (see Figure 2B-15)." [visible in Image 3] Guidance (recommended): - "To minimize wrong-way movements onto freeway or expressway exit ramps, Street Name signs should not be used at the intersection of a freeway or expressway exit ramp with the crossroad to display the name of the freeway or expressway to traffic on the crossroad." (This is a related countermeasure, not one of the three sign types.) Options (permitted): - A Directional assembly with a diagonal downward-pointing arrow (M6-2aP) plaque may be used at the far left-hand corner of an intersection with a freeway or expressway entrance ramp to "distinguish the entrance ramp from an adjoining exit ramp terminal at the same intersection with the conventional road," helping road users avoid entering the wrong ramp. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2B-15 depicts the exit-ramp terminal treatment: paired DO NOT ENTER signs facing the crossroad, back-to-back ONE WAY sign assemblies on both sides of the ramp, and WRONG WAY signs facing potential wrong-way traffic down the exit ramp, plus STOP or YIELD control at the ramp terminal and wrong-way pavement arrows. - [Image 2] This full-page view of Figure 2B-15 ("Example of Application of Regulatory Signing and Pavement Markings at an Exit Ramp Termination to Deter Wrong-Way Entry," Sect. 2B.48) confirms the same three sign types arranged around the exit-ramp/crossroad intersection. - [Image 3] This page shows Section 2B.46, whose Standard mandates the DO NOT ENTER sign at "the intersection of an interchange exit ramp with a crossroad as specified in Section 2B.48 (see Figure 2B-15)," and Figure 2B-13 displaying the R5-1 (DO NOT ENTER), R5-1a (WRONG WAY), and R6-1/R6-2 (ONE WAY) signs. - [Image 4] The table of contents lists Figure 2B-15 ("Example of Application of Regulatory Signing and Pavement Markings at an Exit Ramp Termination to Deter Wrong-Way Entry") and related figures 2B-13 and 2B-17 pairing DO NOT ENTER, WRONG WAY, and ONE WAY signing. - [Image 5] Figure 2D-18's notes direct the reader to "See Section 2B.48 and Figure 2B-15 for an example of regulatory signing and pavement markings at an exit ramp termination to deter wrong-way entry," confirming Section 2B.48 as the governing provision. Citations: - Figure 2B-15 (p.112) - Page 153 - Page 150 - Page 29 - Page 297 - Section 2D.45 Guidance §3 (p.247) - Section 2D.50 Option §3 (p.254)
gold_answer: At least one ONE WAY sign for each crossroad travel direction, at least one DO NOT ENTER sign near the downstream end of the exit ramp, and at least one WRONG WAY sign on the exit ramp facing wrong-way road users are required.
